messages:
Mira Chen: Heads-up — seeing a p95 token-latency regression after the runtime deploy that changed kernel selection heuristics. Impacting /api/v2/generate in prod-us. p95 per-token jumped ~2x for typical 512-seq requests; rough cost-per-token for that route up ~15%.
Kevin Wu: Which revision triggered it? any traces or profiles? @deploy-bot can you confirm rollout id for the kernel selector change? :eyes:
deploy-bot: rollout/2026-03-15-kerselector (rev: abcdef) completed to prod-us at 2026-03-15T02:41:00Z.
Mira Chen: Quick local perf log I grabbed from the canary fleet: 
```
perf_summary:
route: /api/v2/generate
model: redwood-3b-4k
kernel: fused_attn_v2
seq: 512 avg_tok_ms=2.1 p95_tok_ms=4.8  -> previous (standard_matmul) avg_tok_ms=1.1 p95=2.4
batching: observed smaller batches (avg 3 -> 1.7) after heuristic change
kv_cache: miss_rate increased 10% -> 28% for streaming sessions
notes: tail dominated by kernel overhead + increased serialization per-request
```
Lucas Ops: That matches a kernel-selection edge case: fused_attn_v2 is great for very large seq & big batches but adds per-call overhead for small batches. Combined with the batching heuristic that favors latency-first flush, we accidentally reduced avg batch size which amplifies per-token cost.
Sarah ML: The KV miss spike is worrying too. Did the cache key format change or did session affinity/tcp reuse drop? That would increase compute per-token if we re-populate KV frequently.
Mira Chen: I traced the runtime diff — selector now prefers fused_attn_v2 when capability flag true; we didn't weight in "effective_tokens_per_batch" in the cost function. Also the batcher change introduces an earlier flush threshold to hit p50 latency targets, which is shrinking batches for many interactive routes.
Kevin Wu: OK. Ops plan: revert selector in prod-canary, add a gate to prefer standard_matmul for seq < 1024 or avg_batch_size < 4. Can you open a quick PR and rollback? Also we need better metrics: token-level breakdown by kernel + batch_size + kv_hit so we can see where cost comes from.
Mira Chen: Yup — opening rollback PR and a selector patch. Also adding a perf test matrix to CI for fused_attn_v2 across batch sizes.
Sarah ML: I'll run offline microbench across batch sizes and seq lengths and post numbers here. We should also instrument the per-token latency with labels (kernel, batch_size_bucket, route, kv_hit) so dashboards can slice.
Kevin Wu: Example PromQL suggestions for dashboards we should add: 
```
# avg token latency by kernel
sum(rate(token_latency_seconds_sum{env=\"prod\"}[1m])) by (kernel) / sum(rate(token_latency_seconds_count{env=\"prod\"}[1m])) by (kernel)

# batch size p95 per route
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(batch_size_bucket{env=\"prod\"}[5m])) by (le, route))
```
Mira Chen: Also need a nightly reconciliation job to align token accounting with billing. Current mismatch is partly due to input tokens being weighted differently in billing and our metrics. Proposed SQL for reconciliation: 
```
SELECT route,
       SUM(tokens_generated + tokens_input * 0.5) as tokens_billed,
       SUM(cost_usd) / SUM(tokens_billed) as cost_per_token
FROM billing_events
WHERE ts >= '2026-03-01'
GROUP BY route
ORDER BY cost_per_token DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
Lucas Ops: Nice. Action items I propose: 
- rollback kernel selector in canary immediately
- patch selector rule (prefer standard_matmul for seq < 1024 OR avg_batch_size < 4)
- add token-level labels: kernel, batch_size_bucket, kv_hit to runtime metrics
- add Grafana panels: token_latency_by_kernel, avg_batch_size_by_route, kv_miss_rate, cost_per_token_by_route
- add alert: if p95_token_latency > 1.2x baseline for 10m for any top-10 route
- daily cost-per-token job to compute unit economics per route and surface top regressions

Mira Chen: I'll open the rollback PR & selector patch now and assign the dashboard tickets. @Sarah ML can you run the microbench and share CSV?
Sarah ML: On it, starting runs now — will attach CSV in ~30m. I'll test fused_attn_v2 vs standard_matmul across batch sizes [1,2,4,8,16] and seq [128,512,2048].
Kevin Wu: Thanks. Once we have labeled metrics we can create a per-route leaderboard: cost_per_token, p50/p95 token latency, avg_batch_size. That will help product owners prioritize optimizations.
Mira Chen: One more note — let's include billing metadata in the token metrics (billing_tier, customer_type) so the daily job can slice unit economics by customer segment.
Lucas Ops: Agree. I'll add instrumentation spec in the PR description.
deploy-bot: rollback/2026-03-15-kerselector (rev: abcdef) triggered by Kevin Wu -> staging at 2026-03-15T03:10:12Z.
Mira Chen: Thanks all. Will post followups (CI microbench results + dashboard PR) in this thread. :thumbsup:
